metadata.title: Veteran Analyst Doubles Down on Massive Palantir Stock Call

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) could eventually become a $1 trillion company, according to longtime technology analyst Daniel Ives, a call that would require roughly 141% upside from the AI software company's current $414.7 billion market value. The thesis rests on Palantir maintaining extraordinary commercial growth as enterprises move from experimenting with artificial intelligence to deploying it across real-world operations, but the stock's already demanding valuation leaves little room for execution mistakes.
Ives reiterated the view at the Future Proof Conference in Huntington Beach, California. He had previously argued in April that Palantir could reach a $1 trillion valuation within two to three years.
Palantir's recent growth helps explain the optimism.
Second-quarter revenue surged 93% year over year to $1.94 billion, while U.S. commercial revenue jumped 149% to $764 million. Overall commercial revenue increased 110%, showing that growth is increasingly coming from private-sector customers rather than relying predominantly on government contracts.
Management also raised its 2026 revenue outlook to between $8.15 billion and $8.158 billion, implying roughly 82% growth at the midpoint. U.S. commercial revenue is expected to increase at least 134%.
Palantir's Artificial Intelligence Platform remains central to that expansion, helping customers connect AI models with existing data and operational workflows.
Wall Street is also becoming more constructive. UBS analyst Karl Keirstead recently lifted his price target to $250 from $220 while maintaining a Buy rating after meetings with customers and management at AIPCon.
Investors Takeaway
The $1 trillion thesis ultimately depends on whether Palantir can sustain hypergrowth long enough to justify its premium valuation.
The stock trades at roughly 78 times forward earnings and more than 72 times trailing sales, meaning slowing growth could trigger substantial multiple compression.
Investors should watch U.S. commercial growth, customer expansion, deal sizes and whether full-year guidance keeps moving higher. Continued growth near current levels would strengthen Ives' case.
The biggest risk is that expectations are already exceptionally high. Palantir does not simply need strong results; it likely needs repeated earnings beats and sustained AI adoption to grow into a valuation approaching $1 trillion.
